messages:
Rita (devex): quick heads-up — found a reproducible parity issue between python sdk streaming chat and direct REST streaming. Chunks come in reversed order and we lose the final \"done\" event in the SDK stream.
Liam (py-sdk): that's scary. Can you paste minimal repros (curl + sdk snippet)?
Rita (devex): curl that works (server sends chunked events in order, ends with event: done):
```bash
curl -i -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize x"}],"max_tokens":128,"temperature":0.2}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```
Rita (devex): python sdk that shows the bug:
```py
from redwood import Redwood
c = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('TOKEN'))
for chunk in c.chat.stream(model='rwd-chat-v1', messages=[{"role":"user","content":"summarize x"}], maxTokens=128, temperature=0.2):
    print(chunk)
```
Rita (devex): Observed: SDK logs chunks in reverse order and no final DONE event. If I call REST curl the order is correct and there is a final `event: done`.
Maya (eng-runtime): curious — in the SDK trace do you see any buffer/queue code that might reorder events?
Rita (devex): captured raw tcp stream from proxy. REST raw shows: chunk1 -> chunk2 -> done. SDK raw shows the same bytes but the SDK layer yields chunk2 then chunk1 then closes. So it's SDK-side reordering.
Liam (py-sdk): thanks, that points to our internal chunk aggregator. Also noticed you passed `maxTokens` in camelCase in SDK example — our SDK currently accepts snake_case and lowerCamel in places, but server expects `max_tokens`. If the SDK renames to `maxTokens` in the JSON body the server ignores it and falls back to default (64) causing early truncation in some runs. That could explain missing content sometimes.
Rita (devex): ah interesting — I tried `max_tokens` vs `maxTokens`; behaviour changed. So two separate issues: (1) param name mapping -> defaulting/truncation; (2) stream event ordering in the aggregator.
QA-Kate: I can add a unit+integration: assert body JSON keys exactly match curl (max_tokens, temperature, etc) and add an e2e stream-order test using a deterministic mock server that emits numbered chunks.
Liam (py-sdk): action plan: 1) stop automatic camelCase mapping for body keys and send raw kwargs -> snake_case per API spec; 2) fix chunk aggregator ordering (probably from async task scheduling race when combining event loop callbacks). I'll open PRs.
PR-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood/sdk-python/pull/812 "fix: preserve API snake_case keys + fix stream ordering" by liam (CI running).
Arjun (pm): How bad is customer impact? Any support tickets?
Rita (devex): We got one new user report: quickstart chat appears to truncate replies and sometimes duplicates last sentence — would match these two bugs. I marked support ticket #5981.
Maya (eng-runtime): Also a subtle auth mismatch I saw earlier in an unrelated report: some SDKs set ephemeral-refresh header `X-Redwood-Refresh` and fallback to `Authorization: Token <val>` during refresh that older gateways treat as unknown. REST uses Authorization: Bearer exclusively. Can we unify?
Liam (py-sdk): yeah we have a tiny lib that tries both for backwards compatibility. I'll remove `Token` fallback and make refresh header explicit `Authorization: Bearer <token>` for all flows.
QA-Kate: Regression test matrix: python sdk v0.10.0 should be validated vs curl for these endpoints: chat/stream, chat, embeddings. I'll add tests to CI job `sdk-parity-e2e` and mark them as non-flaky initially.
Rita (devex): also flag sample-apps quickstart chat in the docs — it currently shows `maxTokens` in example which encouraged users to use camelCase. I'll send a docs PR to use `max_tokens` and include a note about streaming clients.
Arjun (pm): Prioritize patch release if CI is green. This affects onboarding and our quickstarts. Also update release notes with breaking change if we remove camelCase mapping.
Liam (py-sdk): will add a compatibility shim: for a single patch release we'll accept both but log a deprecation warning. Long-term we'll only send snake_case. Plan: patch (0.10.1) with fixes + deprecation warnings, then 0.11.0 remove shim.
PR-bot: CI passed for PR #812 — merging to main.
Liam (py-sdk): released v0.10.1: "fix: stream chunk ordering; fix: send snake_case keys; fix: auth scheme; add parity tests + deprecation warnings"
Rita (devex): verified quickstart chat works with 0.10.1 and the sample-app no longer truncates. Thanks team.
Arjun (pm): Great. Follow-ups: QA-Kate to monitor flaky suite for 48h, Liam to draft deprecation note, Rita to update sample-apps and docs.
QA-Kate: added to monitoring board.
